hero.filename: F-4D with T-28 at Ubon RTAFB 1972.jpg
hero.title: File:F-4D with T-28 at Ubon RTAFB 1972.jpg
hero.credit: scan from Dana Bell: Air War over Vietnam. Volume IV. Arms & Armour Press, London (UK), 1985. ISBN 0-85368-635-1, p. 23. USAF cited as source.
hero.source: F-4D with T-28 at Ubon RTAFB 1972
hero.description: A U.S. Air Force McDonnell Douglas F-4D Phantom II (s/n 66-8738) from the 497th Tactical Fighter Squadron, 8th Tactical Fighter Wing has its weapons armed at a 'last chance' checkpoint at Ubon Royal Thai Air Force Base prior to a mission in North Vietnam in September 1972. A Royal Thai Air Force North American T-28D Trojan is also waiting for take-off. The black-bellied F-4D 66-8738 was equipped with AN/ARN-92 LORAN-D equipment (note antenna) and was one of only two F-4Ds fitted with the AVQ-11 Pave Sword precision attack sensor. However, it was shot down by a North Vietnamese Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21 with an Atoll-missile on 5 October 1972. The crew was taken prisoner but was released in 1973. The Thai T-28D (former U.S. Navy T-28B, BuNo 137802) was preserved at the RTAFB Phitsanulok, painted as "46101".
categories: F-4 Phantom II in the Vietnam War

gallery.filename: Sabre Mk32s RAAF in Thailand early 1960s.jpg
gallery.title: File:Sabre Mk32s RAAF in Thailand early 1960s.jpg
gallery.credit: U.S. Air Force photo from Dana Bell: Air War over Vietnam IV. London, Arms&Armour Press 1984, p. 10. ISBN 0-85368-635-1. Cited as USAF photo.
gallery.source: Sabre Mk32s RAAF in Thailand early 1960s
gallery.description: Royal Australian Air Force Commonwealth Aircraft Sabre Mk.32 fighters (A94-964, A94-982) are prepared for joint exercises with the U.S. Air Force and the Royal Thai Air Force in the early 1960s. A94-964 crashed in Thailand in April 1963 and was used for spare parts, A94-982 is today on display at the RAAF Forest Hill Museum, Wagga Wagga, New South Wales (Australia).
categories: Royal Australian Air Force in the Vietnam War
